newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to unveil new finance firms merger rules.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to unveil new finance firms merger rules.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Monday the government would unveil new finance company merger guidelines this week in a bid to encourage consolidation in the industry.
Amnuay told reporters the regulations would include incentives for merged finance firms to upgrade into full commercial banks.

The minister said that between two to five new bank licenses would be made available. These would be available for finance institution groups that have minimum assets of 150 billion baht ($6 billion).
He also said merged companies with less combined assets could seek to undertake a wider scope of business including taking savings deposits, provide foreign exchange and trade financing services.

The new rules to be announced follow the recent collapse of a planned merger between Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc which the government earlier hoped would serve as a model for similar business alliances among Thailand's 91 finance firms.

The two institutions had cited tax and legal complications as reasons for the failure of their planned deal. Analysts had said new and more viable rules were needed to spark more consolidation in the industry.
The government has worked hard to boost and revamp the battered finance sector which has been severely hit by growing non-performing loans to the ailing property sector.
Amnuay said applicants for new domestic bank licenses must meet asset, capital and other qualifications to ensure that they could contribute to future stability in the financial sector.
